headline: A code outside CIA headquarters that went unsolved for 35 years.
slides: Artist Jim Sanborn installed Kryptos, a copper sculpture of encrypted text, at CIA headquarters.
He built the codes with Ed Scheidt, a retiring head of the CIA's cryptographic center.
Three of its four messages were cracked in the 1990s.
The fourth passage beat everyone, despite decades of hints from Sanborn himself.
Two writers found K4's plain text in Sanborn's papers at the Smithsonian. They found it, they didn't crack it.
Sanborn's archive, with the answer, sold at auction to an anonymous buyer for $963,000.
